AUDIO IMPORTANT:

*I take the audio from the video and save it to the output video directly for quality control. but also pass the audio through the workflow to help the mouth movements*

*testing pushing video audio through ref to video node ref_video_audio_0 slot to see if it keeps mouth movements which its losing at distance.*

if there is no audio in your video-in then it errors. 

If you have silent video, you will need to provide audio in of some kind to run the workflow, even if you dont include it in the output video. Use the audio loader to load in a random mp3 (e.g. 10 seconds of music or ambient silence) and set duration to match your inbound video. swithc the audio vae encoder to use this not the video. This should then work.

NOTE: I found if I prompt for "non_diegetic_music:" it will then use it rather than the audio, so make sure to put "N/A" in any audio descriptors for the prompt if you want to keep the audio you are loading in.

# MarkDKBerry.com

YouTube: [https://www.youtube.com/@markdkberry](https://www.youtube.com/@markdkberry)

Patreon: [https://www.patreon.com/c/AIMakingMovies](https://www.patreon.com/c/AIMakingMovies)

Workflows: [https://github.com/mdkberry/comfyui_workflows](https://github.com/mdkberry/comfyui_workflows)

---

**You will need to install [https://github.com/ckinpdx/ComfyUI-MMH3Tools](https://github.com/ckinpdx/ComfyUI-MMH3Tools) for this workflow.** If you have a Low or MidVRAM (12GB VRAM) card this workflow should work for you, if you have a bigger card, you might want to test ckinpdx upscale workflows instead. 

It works by "context window" splitting the total frames (e.g. 192 frame video split to two segments, so you can get to the magical 2mp for 8 second clips as I did in tests, even on a 3060 RTX. You max VRAM is then used on each split segment thus giving you better reach. Amazingly it was still faster than my other upscaler workflows.

---

**Updated**: 25th August 2026. *(replaced batch image list node with MMH3 Image List node. changed sampler and sigma settings .)*

**Useage**: *Single pass v2v pixel space upscaler with context windows to split use of the VRAM across multiple segments, making higher resolution possible for longer clips on lowerVRAM.*


---

## USING THIS WORKFLOW

***UPDATE NOTE: I could get 3mp for 8 second video in 30 mins, using pika lora, set 2 step manual sigmas to 0.7, 0.49, 0 with euler sampler, attempts to try the clownscheduler oomed at 3mp and occasional runs failed but its the best I have achieved so far - Mark, 2n Nov 2026.)***


**Get a structural video made elsewhere, then import it here for detailing.** (its best if you use fairly high quality result coming in, I found 1824 x 736 was good that needed eyes fixing a bit and blemishes. For stronger fixing, you might need to increase denoise or steps. I havent tested it for that yet.)

**Set to chosen megapixel upscale size I can do 2mp for 8 seconds in this workflow** (see the notes beside the video import node). Resize if you need to reduce the inbound video, upscale if you need to increase it. Size it to fit your VRAM and avoid ooms.

**I've been leaving the width and height of the actual "H3 Reference To Video Model" Node set to 1mp**. We know it to be the size the H3 model was trained on. But the important bit is the size of your inbound video and what you resize that to.

**The frame count of the video-in is used to define the length**, as such the duration has been disabled in this workflow. 

**Since this uses context windows, oom from longer videos is mitigated**. I have only tested 8 seconds long video so far and could get to 2mp with only 10.5GB VRAM being used. There is a spike going into  the sampler but it didnt oom on my setup with this workflow. Context windows is the reason for this. Its suprisingly fast, considering that, I was expecting it to take a lot longer.

**Make a new prompt and be sure to target the ref images correctly**. 

I am getting 8 second video done in 26 mins to 2mp. Longer clip length will probably work too due to the "context windows" from the ckinpdx custom node.

## ISSUES:

- You must provide audio to the workflow either from the inbound video, or by providing your own audio file. I have put a audio loader in there which you can reconnect (yellow vrs red reroute connector).

subject_definitions:
<Picture 1> is the first frame of [Shot 1] and the blocking reference only. It is a lower-quality, medium-wide 21:9 frame in the same gothic drawing room from a new camera position: the bald man in the black suit sits at centre in a carved armchair mid-sip with a wine glass at his lips, the brunette in the red velvet gown stands behind and just left of him, and the blonde in the blue velvet gown sits in the right foreground in profile, facing left toward him. A stone fireplace is behind them. Character likeness comes from the character references, not from the image quality of <Picture 1>.
<Subject 1> is the bald middle-aged man in <Picture 2>, shown full length and front facing in a black suit, white shirt and slim black tie, with a stern, weathered face.
<Subject 2> is the long-haired blonde woman in <Picture 3>, shown full length, front facing and barefoot in a blue velvet wrap gown with a deep V neckline.
<Subject 3> is the dark-haired brunette woman in <Picture 4>, shown full length, front facing and barefoot in a burgundy-red velvet gown.
<Subject 4> is the decaying gothic mansion drawing room in <Picture 1>, with a pale carved stone fireplace with a warm glowing fire, a mantel crowded with white pillar candles, a standing candelabra at left, a framed dark portrait painting on the peeling ochre plaster wall at upper right, and a thick worn carpet underfoot.
<Audio 1> is the voice-timbre reference for <Subject 3> (S2), a posh English female voice, slightly husky.
<Audio 2> is the voice-timbre reference for <Subject 1> (S1), a deep, gravelly American male voice.
<Audio 3> is the voice-timbre reference for <Subject 2> (S3), a posh English female voice.

summary:
[keyframe completion + reference generation + audio reference] A single continuous 15-second dialogue shot of a 1970s Hammer-style sapphic vampire gothic scene, beginning from <Picture 1>. <Subject 1> lowers his glass, startled by how good the wine tastes, laughs and banters with the two vampire women <Subject 3> and <Subject 2>, who watch him with quiet predatory interest while he remains unaware. The camera makes a very slow, smooth pull-back to a balanced three-shot. The voices follow <Audio 2>, <Audio 1> and <Audio 3> as timbre references only. There is no music.

retention_analysis:
<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] first frame): partially_preserved - the camera angle, blocking, seating positions and set are kept, while character likeness and costume detail follow the character references rather than the low image quality.
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - face, bald head, black suit, white shirt, black tie and seated posture are retained.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - long straight blonde hair, blue velvet gown and pale complexion are retained.
<Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - dark wavy hair and burgundy velvet gown are retained.
<Subject 4> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - fireplace, candles, candelabra, portrait and decayed walls are retained.
<Audio 1>: reference - the posh, slightly husky English timbre guides <Subject 3>'s line without copying the source signal.
<Audio 2>: reference - the deep, gravelly American timbre guides <Subject 1>'s lines without copying the source signal.
<Audio 3>: reference - the posh English female timbre guides <Subject 2>'s line without copying the source signal.

detailed_description:
The target video is a 1970s Hammer Horror gothic vampire scene, shot on Panasonic VariCam 35, ultra-smooth 180-degree shutter, shallow depth of field, anamorphic lens flare, Hammer Horror film aesthetic, Eastmancolor film stock, warm pushed saturation, slightly overexposed highlights, deep crushed shadows, lush theatrical lighting, gothic British period atmosphere, 1960s-1970s Bray Studios production design, velvet textures and rich decay, soft focus on backgrounds, cinematic 21:9 Ultrawide, smooth filmic motion, no digital sharpness, organic grain structure.
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1>, a medium-wide frame in <Subject 4>. Throughout the 15 seconds the camera performs one extremely slow, smooth dolly back with no shake and no sudden speed change, easing from the tight medium framing out to a balanced wider three-shot with the fireplace, mantel candles and portrait fully framed. <Subject 1>, the bald man in the black suit, sits at centre in the carved armchair with the wine glass at his lips. <Subject 3>, the brunette in the burgundy gown, stands behind and left of him with her left hand resting lightly on the chair back and a faint knowing smile. <Subject 2>, the blonde in the blue velvet gown, sits in the right foreground in profile, her right hand resting calmly on the chair arm, her eyes fixed on him. Neither woman drinks. In the first two seconds <Subject 1> lowers the glass and looks down into it, brows lifting, plainly taken aback at how good the wine tastes, while both women simply observe him in silence. About three seconds in he gives a light, warm laugh and raises his eyes to look at both women in turn. Around four seconds in <Subject 1> (S1) says in the deep gravelly American voice referenced from <Audio 2>, with amused disbelief, <d>[English] You two are something else. Do you treat all your guests like this?</d> About eight seconds in, <Subject 3> (S2) holds his gaze, tilts her head and replies slowly in the posh, slightly husky English voice referenced from <Audio 1>, <d>[English] Only the ones that suit our tastes.</d> Her smile deepens and <Subject 2> glances at her. Around ten seconds in, <Subject 1> lets his eyes wander round the room, up to the mantel candles, across to the portrait and the candelabra, and says in the same gravelly voice, easy and unsuspecting, <d>[English] You should turn this place into a hotel. You'd make a killing.</d> Around thirteen seconds in, <Subject 2> (S3) turns her gaze to him and says softly in the posh English female voice referenced from <Audio 3>, <d>[English] That would be a feast.</d> <Subject 1> chuckles, still oblivious, as the two women hold their calm, watchful stares and the shot ends silently on the wider three-shot. All hands remain anatomically clear and attached to their sleeves. There are no footsteps, since everyone stays in place.

overall_soundscape:
A hushed, cavernous room tone runs throughout, with soft crackling and popping from the fire, faint candle flutter, gentle velvet and suit-fabric rustles, a creak of the carved chair, the soft touch of the glass being lowered and the faint sound of a swallow. There are no footstep sounds.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A

widgets_values:
LowVRAM you need chunk feed forward and LowVRAM attention on else you'll probably oom when it hits the sampler at 2mp.

I have tried different loras, choose to suit your speedup preferences.

default manual sigmas: 0.7,0.49,0
if losing mouth movements try: 0.50, 0.25, 0

set ModelSampling node shift_audio to 3 if working, 4 if losing mouth movements.

## LORA TESTS 9th NOVEMBER 2026 (json v7 onwards)

*testing needs to be below 0.9 on first sigma else it removes lipsync mouth movements.*
	
**sigmas: 0.7, 0.49, 0. lcm sampler.** (at only 2 steps this is euler is best option).
	
- flashgen str 0.7 **one of the best equal with drbaph str 0.8** 
- "drbaph turbo v4 step600 ema pruned". str 0.8 **this was the best equal with flashgen I think. more testing on different examples needed.**

- pika str 1.0 **okay but eyes not fixing** on the dude
- pdmd 2-step (caused issues at 1.0) str 0.5 (**fixes his eyes but has a dappled plastic issue,** but less at low str, try even less strength. also try this in a upscaler before the final polish stage.)
- pdmd 2-step str 0.3 (trying to reduce plastic effect. **a lot better but just looks a bit cheap and a bit plastic**)
- taomate str 0.5 (**quite good** but maybe tweaks to others would beat it)
- "drbaph turbo v4 step600 ema pruned". str 0.5 (**surprisingly good, if I can tweak it one better this might be the winner**)
